content: 1. Rifampin and Ethinyl Estradiol: Rifampin reduces the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by inducing the CYP3A4 enzyme, which accelerates its metabolism in the liver and intestines. This can decrease the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, a non-hormonal contraceptive method should be used. 2. Rifapentine and Ethinyl Estradiol/Norethindrone Acetate: Rifapentine also induces CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol and norethindrone acetate. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable during co-administration, and non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Additionally, menstrual irregularities such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia may occur. 3. Ritonavir and Ethinyl Estradiol: Ritonavir can either increase or decrease estrogen plasma levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 4. Ferrous Fumarate and Tetracycline: Ferrous fumarate decreases tetracycline absorption in the gastrointestinal tract, reducing its effectiveness. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Alternative drugs or careful monitoring are advised. 5. St. John’s Wort and Ethinyl Estradiol: St. John’s Wort induces CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol. Hormonal contraceptives may become less effective, and non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 6. Sugammadex and Ethinyl Estradiol: A bolus dose of sugammadex is equivalent to missing one or more doses of hormonal contraceptives. Patients should use an additional non-hormonal contraceptive method for the next 7 days. 7. Tipranavir and Ethinyl Estradiol: Tipranavir can cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 8. Topiramate and Ethinyl Estradiol/Norethindrone Acetate: Topiramate induces CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing the levels and effects of these hormones. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable, and non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 9. Tovorafenib and Ethinyl Estradiol: Tovorafenib induces CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods should be used during co-administration and for 28 days after discontinuation. 10. Tucatinib and Ethinyl Estradiol: Tucatinib inhibits CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol. Avoid co-administration with CYP3A substrates unless necessary, and adjust the dose of the substrate accordingly. 11. Norethindrone Acetate and Albiglutide: Hormonal contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 12. Ethinyl Estradiol and Albiglutide: Similar to norethindrone acetate, ethinyl estradiol may impair glucose tolerance and reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications. Monitor glycemic control. 13. Ethinyl Estradiol and Alosetron: Ethinyl estradiol inhibits CYP1A2 metabolism, increasing the levels and effects of alosetron. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Aluminum Hydroxide and Ferrous Fumarate: Aluminum hydroxide increases gastric pH, reducing the absorption and effectiveness of ferrous fumarate. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 15. Ethinyl Estradiol and Alprazolam: Ethinyl estradiol inhibits the metabolism of alprazolam, increasing its serum concentrations. Use caution and monitor for potential benzodiazepine-related side effects. 16. Ethinyl Estradiol and Aminocaproic Acid: Concomitant use may lead to additive hypercoagulability. Estrogens increase clotting factor production, while aminocaproic acid inhibits fibrinolysis. Use caution and monitor for thrombotic events. 17. Amoxicillin and Ethinyl Estradiol: Amoxicillin may alter intestinal flora, potentially reducing the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Ampicillin and Ethinyl Estradiol: Similar to amoxicillin, ampicillin may reduce the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. Use caution and monitor. 19. Artemether/Lumefantrine and Ethinyl Estradiol: This combination induces CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol. Use caution and monitor. 20. Atazanavir and Norethindrone Acetate: Atazanavir and norethindrone acetate may reduce each other’s effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 21. Ethinyl Estradiol and Atogepant: Ethinyl estradiol inhibits CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the levels and effects of atogepant. Use caution and monitor. 22. Atorvastatin and Ethinyl Estradiol: Atorvastatin increases the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor. 23. Ethinyl Estradiol and Axitinib: Ethinyl estradiol inhibits CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing the levels and effects of axitinib. Use caution and monitor. 24. Ethinyl Estradiol and Bendamustine: Ethinyl estradiol inhibits CYP1A2 metabolism, increasing the levels and effects of bendamustine. Use caution and monitor. 25. Ferrous Fumarate and Bictegravir: Ferrous fumarate reduces the absorption of bictegravir in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer bictegravir with food or separate administration by at least 2 hours. 26. Ethinyl Estradiol and Caffeine: Ethinyl estradiol inhibits CYP1A2 metabolism, increasing the levels and effects of caffeine. Use caution and monitor. 27. Calcium Carbonate and Ferrous Fumarate: Calcium carbonate increases gastric pH, reducing the absorption and effectiveness of ferrous fumarate. Use caution and monitor. 28. Cefaclor and Ethinyl Estradiol: Cefaclor may alter intestinal flora, potentially reducing the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Cefadroxil and Ethinyl Estradiol: Similar to cefaclor, cefadroxil may reduce the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. Use caution and monitor. 30. Cefazolin and Ethinyl Estradiol: Similar to other cephalosporins, cefazolin may reduce the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. Use caution and monitor. 31. Cefdinir and Ethinyl Estradiol: Cefdinir may alter intestinal flora, potentially reducing the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol. Use caution and monitor. 32. Cefepime and Ethinyl Estradiol: Similar to other cephalosporins, cefepime may reduce the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. Use caution and monitor. 33. Cefepime/Enmetazobactam and Ethinyl Estradiol: This combination may alter intestinal flora, potentially reducing the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol. Use caution and monitor. 34. Cefixime and Ethinyl Estradiol: Similar to other cephalosporins, cefixime may reduce the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. Use caution and monitor. 35. Cefotaxime and Ethinyl Estradiol: Cefotaxime may alter intestinal flora, potentially reducing the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol. Use caution and monitor. 36. Cefprozil and Ethinyl Estradiol: Similar to other cephalosporins, cefprozil may reduce the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. Use caution and monitor. 37. Ceftazidime and Ethinyl Estradiol: Ceftazidime may alter intestinal flora, potentially reducing the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol. Use caution and monitor. 38. Ceftibuten and Ethinyl Estradiol: Similar to other cephalosporins, ceftibuten may reduce the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. Use caution and monitor. 39. Cefuroxime and Ethinyl Estradiol: Cefuroxime may alter intestinal flora, potentially reducing the effectiveness of ethinyl estradiol. Use caution and monitor. 40. Cenobamate and Ethinyl Estradiol/Norethindrone Acetate: Cenobamate induces CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing the levels and effects of these hormones. Modify therapy or monitor closely.
